There is currently no way to schedule coroutines or callbacks directly from a different process (such as one started with multiprocessing). May 17, 2024 - In Python’s asynchronous programming model, a Future is a low-level awaitable object that represents an eventual result of an asynchronous operation. When you create a Future, you're essentially declaring a placeholder for a result that will be available at some point in the future. Futures are a crucial part of the asyncio library, allowing for fine-grained control over asynchronous operations.
